verdict.rationale: PlanetScale documents its own agent-facing paths for database work: a hosted MCP server that connects agents to databases with tools, and a `pscale sql` command for non-interactive SQL by agents. Service tokens can authenticate the MCP server for headless agents. However, nothing in the evidence shows tools scoped or labeled to separate read-only from destructive actions, so the safety half of the story is unevidenced. Missing for 10: documented read-only vs destructive tool separation, permission scoping of MCP or service-token access for SQL/schema operations, schema-change tooling exposed to agents, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can run SQL and schema operations through scoped tools that distinguish read-only from destructive actions, so I can safely delegate database work

citations.quote: Run non-interactive SQL for agents and scripts (`pscale sql`)
Connect Claude, Cursor, Notion, and other MCP-compatible tools to your PlanetScale databases and Insights
The hosted MCP server provides access to database information and tools
Use a PlanetScale service token to authenticate the hosted MCP server in CI, headless agents, and clients that send a custom HTTP header
